Samantha —

Thanks for the files and the clear asks. Quick read-through and next steps from our side:

1) High-level: We can accommodate the transfer addendum language in principle but need to confirm hosting/export routing implications with infra/ops. I’ve flagged the specific clause (4b).

2) Roles: Ben and I started a short controller/processor crosswalk in the attached matrix — see column "Redwood role note". There are two places where delegation is ambiguous (Section 2.1 and 5.3).

3) Timeline: Legal review + infra check — target is 72 hours. That puts us to Friday EOD as requested, but if infra needs a host-change or VPC exception the timeline could extend.

Action items I’m assigning now:
- Jonas Weber (Legal Ops) — I asked him to review the redlines and confirm any MSA/order-form tieouts required.
- Ben Carter (Privacy) — can you re-run the export matrix and confirm if any region-level routing surcharge would be required?

Please expect a consolidated note from us by Thursday midday. If you need faster escalation to SLA/exec, tell me and I’ll loop in legal leadership.

On attachments: I pulled the two into our internal review folder and left a short comment set in the doc for the two ambiguous delegation spots.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@novaprod.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@novaprod.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Updated DPA redlines + export addendum (tracking)

Irene / Ben / Samantha —

I reviewed Novaprod_DPA_redline_v3.docx and the export_matrix_v2.xlsx. High-level notes:

- Clause 4b (restricted export pathways): redline language is acceptable with two edits to avoid overbroad obligations in incident response. I’ve annotated the doc with suggested alternate wording (comments labeled JW-1 and JW-2).
- Delegation ambiguity (2.1 / 5.3): propose a short bridging paragraph that clarifies Redwood remains processor for the model inference pipeline; customer remains controller for input PII. That should resolve the recursion ask without enlarge our operational burden.
- MSA/order-form: we will not need an MSA rewrite if Novaprod accepts the addendum as a DPA annex; we will, however, require a running order-form note that ties the DPA annex to the specific order (I recommend a two-line addendum in the order form referencing the DPA doc and effective date).

Ops check needed: can Ben confirm whether the export_matrix indicates any non-standard routing (e.g., on-prem export or APAC region egress) that would trigger additional hosting controls? If yes, we should memo that as a deployment exception to the DPA and outline the change in the order form.

I can sign off on the legal redline edits by Thursday morning if Ops confirms no hosting exception.

Jonas Weber
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@novaprod.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Updated DPA redlines + export addendum (tracking)

Quick update from Ops/Privacy: we re-ran the export matrix against our current hosting topology. Results:

- All customer-facing inference requests for Novaprod will be processed in the EU region by default (no APAC egress).
- There is one integration connector that pushes aggregated logs to a third-party analytics vendor in US; that connector can be turned off or routed to an EU-only vendor and we recommend routing to EU to satisfy the stricter transfer controls.
- No VPC or on-prem exceptions required. No surcharge expected.

Recommendation: accept Jonas' language changes (JW-1/JW-2) and include a one-line order-form tie that references DPA annex (effective date = date of signature). We can confirm final text by Thursday EOD.

Ben Carter
Senior Privacy Engineer | Redwood Inference
